data.body:
USER DIRECTIVE (mid-run): fold the follow-up tickets into the epic.

Surfaced the consequence before acting: making the 14 mirror tickets CHILDREN of 87cb would trip
rebar's open-children guard and hold the epic open until all 14 mirrors are actually fixed — days
to weeks of follow-on work — even though epic AC2 treats a live mirror as dispositioned once it
'is either gated/generated OR has a linked child/discovered_from ticket', i.e. FILING is the bar.
User chose the recommended option: a separate remediation epic.

DONE: created epic undamaged-murderous-horse (f79d-0d71-0fd7-439f) 'Track I — representation-mirror
remediation (14 mirrors from the sweep)', linked relates_to 87cb, declared no-file-impact (container
epic). Reparenting the 14 follow-ups under it. Track I stays closeable this run; the remediation work
gets a real epic home with a recommended order (F1 silent data loss -> F12 drifted-now + false gate
claim -> F13 one-line reuse of an existing validator) and a standing caution that the inventory's 9
DISTINCT CONCEPT rejections must not be collapsed by a well-meaning fix.

VERIFICATION CORRECTION: my first AC3 probe reported '0 discovered_from links' and was WRONG — I
queried the sweep task's own deps, but the link is recorded as an OUTBOUND discovered_from on each
CHILD pointing at f9b9 (confirmed on 545a: deps=[{target_id: f9b9..., relation: discovered_from}]).
That is the correct direction and AC3 is satisfied. Worth noting because 'rebar deps <task>' does not
surface inbound edges in its output shape, so the naive check reads as a false negative.

14 TICKETS FILED: 545a(F1) fd6b(F12) 0d3c(F13) 62eb(F5) e755(F3) cacb(F4) a691(F10) 6850(F2)
a516(F6) ce8f(F7) 91b0(F8) 70f5(F9) 1daf(F11) 0af1(F14). Types: bug for the 5 already-drifted
(F12,F5,F3,F4,F10), task for the 9 preventive.

9ca8 RE-REVIEW #1 CAME BACK BLOCK — one sharp, correct finding (G6) against MY remediation, not the
original plan: a boolean-coerced _SECTIONS entry is counted by BOTH the config_key detector and the
feature_flag detector, so one new boolean config key yields TWO (kind,name) baseline entries at a
single definition site, and my per-kind marker form could not express a two-kind justification.
FIXED by making the seven kinds a PARTITION: feature_flag claims the boolean entries, config_key
claims only the non-boolean remainder (103 keys = 27 + 76), plus a new AC1 requiring a test that the
seven detector name-sets are pairwise disjoint so a future detector cannot reintroduce overlap.
Also split 6 compound ACs (advisory P6) into 11 atomic ones and gave every AC a 'Verified by' clause
(advisory E6). Re-review #2 running.
